blockers.quote: Last line inside the image: tonight, think who you would have paid
blockers.why: Check #12. This is a lesson aimed at the viewer, a teacher's closing instruction, not a real line inside the last image. audience.md lists a line that sounds like a teacher as a reason Riya leaves. It also tells her what to do with the story just after the picture has shown it.
blockers.fix: End on the picture, with Arthur dry and warm: "Two rings. He picks up." Optionally a bubble of four words or fewer, such as "Hey. Thinking of you?" Cut "tonight, think who you would have paid". If a viewer-facing line stays, make it a concrete thing she'll see tomorrow, inside the image, not an instruction.

suggestions.quote: The turn breaks the planted belief that the money says how much they care
suggestions.fix: In the script, don't have Arthur say that the money is not care. Show the empty Sent column and let a short, flat line carry it, e.g. "Mom's column. Nearly empty. Yours." The viewer does the sum.
As a spoken line, give it a hushed, quiet delivery and keep it as a fragment: "Sent. Mom. Almost nothing." Don't add "and that hurts".

suggestions.quote: has stopped, and you can't say when
suggestions.fix: Land it as a complete thought, since this is the cost beat: "He stopped paying, and you never noticed when." Direct it as quiet and a little surprised. No comment on how it feels.

suggestions.quote: your mother pays every four minutes
suggestions.fix: Spoken form for say.yaml: "every four minutes" (words, not a digit). Keep the contraction and the fast rhythm: "Crush? Nothing. Mom? Every four minutes." Direct it as amused, then warm.
Spoken form for say.yaml: "gill-oh-vich", "MED-vek", "sa-VIT-skee", and "two thousand". In the line, say "a Cornell study" or "psychologists", not the names, so it doesn't turn into a lecture.
Give it a single-breath take at 1.1x with a curious, half-whispered emotion: "What if you got paid... every time someone thought of you?" The title has a natural pause after "paid".

suggestions.quote: Your best photo: three hundred likes, four coins.
suggestions.fix: Keep the numbers as story words ("three hundred", "four"). Write it as a dry aside and let the picture show the gap: "Three hundred likes. Four coins." Direct it as amused and deadpan, with no "disappointing".

suggestions.quote: coins dropping one by one at 2 a.m., every one from mom
suggestions.fix: This is the wordless peak. Give it a HOLD of 8 to 10 seconds with no narration, and put at most one hushed line after it, such as "Two a.m. Still her." Don't name the feeling over it.

suggestions.quote: the question: who is really thinking of you?
suggestions.fix: Spoken, this is an essay-style line. Make it a fragment pair with an immediate answer: "Who's thinking of you? Let's see." Give it a curious, slightly nervous take.

keep.quote: your crush has paid nothing, and your mother pays every four minutes
somewhere a coin we never see drops for him
a skyline of her bar over everyone else's
